analysis:
Both changed files are live-gated test code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live. Neither is production code, so no production attack surface changes.

1) ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (head lines 41-53): when a specification pins soloPrefillStripeTokens, checkpointEnvironment now also sets EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey from the default CBv2SchedulerConfig(). This only shapes the benchmark scheduler geometry. Values are SDK defaults, not external input. The test-only cache env vars (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT, ALLOW_EPHEMERAL, PERSISTENT_KEY) are unchanged, as are the ephemeral/persistent key-mode assertions and root cleanup. The T-041 posture is unaffected: HMAC-keyed names, the 30-minute TTL, salt scoping, the KEK and the DBK3 format are not touched. The dependence on EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey/stepTokenBudgetKey semantics is outside the supplied evidence. A mismatch there would affect benchmark fidelity only, not a security boundary.

2) Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 389-391): the collect() switch gains a .toolCallDelta case that appends delta.completed to toolCalls. This keeps the switch exhaustive after an upstream enum addition. It is test-only and has no authorization, crypto or data-exposure effect.

No changes touch the coordinator-provider wire, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody or the encryption paths (T-008, TB-002, TB-011). No threat-model updates are required. The one unverified integration contract is the new enum case and the factory keys in the unchanged production sources, which were not supplied. This is a minor compile and behavior consistency question, not a security conclusion.
